what_happened: US inflation doubled then stayed above 5% for a decade; real growth stalled.
home_prices: Home prices rose nominally but lost real value as prices ran ahead of incomes
mortgage_rates: 30-yr fixed entered PMMS at 7.38% (1972) and rose through the decade
portfolio: Stocks volatile (S&P 500 lost 37% nominal over 1973-74 — index publisher record; not re-verified this session)
status: verified (CPI); rates and stocks noted per publisher records
notes: Annual averages computed from the BLS monthly CPI-U table.

event: Second oil shock and Volcker disinflation
what_happened: Inflation peaked then was crushed by the highest interest rates of the modern era; two recessions.
home_prices: Nominal home values stayed up in many markets but real values fell; high rates froze sales
mortgage_rates: 30-yr fixed peaked at 18.63% weekly (Oct 9 1981) — all-time PMMS record
portfolio: S&P 500 nominal total return still positive over 1979-82 as inflation fell — publisher record
source_title: NBER U.S. Business Cycle Expansions and Contractions

what_happened: Regional defense-sector recession hit California especially hard; property values fell in real terms.
home_prices: Bay Area prices stagnated/fell through the early 1990s (region-specific)
mortgage_rates: 30-yr fixed fell from ~10.5% (1990) toward ~7% (1993) — PMMS record
source_title: NBER U.S. Business Cycle Expansions and Contractions

what_happened: Technology equity crash; Bay Area employment and rents fell sharply.
cpi_inflation: CPI-U +2.8% (2001) — mild inflation despite equity crash
home_prices: Bay Area home prices dipped briefly in 2001-2002 (regional)
portfolio: S&P 500 fell three years in a row 2000-2002 (publisher record)
source_title: NBER U.S. Business Cycle Expansions and Contractions

event: Global financial crisis and Great Recession
what_happened: Deepest US recession since the 1940s; unemployment peaked near 10% (BLS), housing finance collapsed.
home_prices: National home prices fell ~19% (FHFA all-transactions peak-to-trough) and more on other measures
mortgage_rates: Fed funds cut to near zero; 30-yr fixed fell from ~6.4% to ~5% (PMMS)
portfolio: S&P 500 fell 37% in 2008 then rebounded 26% in 2009 (publisher record)
status: verified (CPI + NBER dates); HPI derived from FHFA series
source_title: NBER U.S. Business Cycle Expansions and Contractions

what_happened: San Francisco metro home prices fell roughly 23% (purchase-only HPI) to 35% (all-transactions HPI) peak (2006-07) to trough (2011-12) depending on measure.
cpi_inflation: CPI mild during the crash years
home_prices: SF metro HPI peak-to-trough about -23% to -35% (measure-dependent); five-year recovery then exceeded +70% (2012-2017)
mortgage_rates: Rates fell through the crash; lending standards tightened
portfolio: Real estate equity wiped out for highly leveraged owners; free-and-clear owners saw no cash-flow interruption
status: derived (from FHFA HPI series; recompute from dataset for exact figures)
notes: FHFA is the official publisher of the HPI; the -23%/-35% range comes from purchase-only vs all-transactions measures of the same official series. Flagged for review.

what_happened: Sharpest but shortest recession on record: two months.
home_prices: Home prices rose during the pandemic (demand shock) despite the recession
mortgage_rates: 30-yr fixed fell to all-time PMMS low 2.65% (week of Jan 7 2021)
portfolio: S&P 500 fell ~34% intramonth (Mar 2020) then recovered within months (publisher record)
notes: NBER: peak Feb 2020 trough Apr 2020 (2 months; shortest on record).

what_happened: Highest inflation in 40 years; fastest rate-hiking cycle since Volcker.
home_prices: US home prices surged in 2021-22 then cooled as rates rose; some metros saw double-digit peak-to-trough declines in 2022-23
mortgage_rates: 30-yr fixed roughly tripled from ~3% (2021) to ~7% (2022-23) — PMMS record
portfolio: S&P 500 fell 19% in 2022 then recovered (publisher record)
notes: Shows inflation can run 3x baseline within two years even after decades of calm.

what_happened: Federal deficit $1.9 trillion (5.8% of GDP) in FY2026; federal debt held by the public 101% of GDP rising to 120% by 2036 — CBO projects debt to exceed its 1946 record by 2030.
cpi_inflation: CBO projects PCE inflation 2.7% (2026 Q4/Q4) and real GDP growth 2.2% — verified
home_prices: CBO does not project house prices; local forecasts are not official
portfolio: Large structural deficits raise the odds of future inflation or rate shocks (analysis note)
source_title: CBO The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036 (Feb 11 2026)
notes: Baseline of record for the projections on this site.

event: Fifty-year inflation record (why constant projections fail)
what_happened: Annual CPI-U inflation over the last 50 completed years ranged from -0.4% (2009) to +13.5% (1980); the 1970s averaged about 7% per decade table and the 2010s under 2%.
cpi_inflation: Full yearly series used in the replay path (see blackswan_paths.csv)
home_prices: Nominal home prices rose in most years but real values fell in the early 1980s early 1990s and 2006-2012
portfolio: Long-run averages hide the sequence: a 40-year average of ~3.9% never actually occurred year after year
notes: The replay scenario literally re-rates these 50 annual inflation rates through the projection.
